name: Residential vs. commercial interior painting considerations
headline: Residential vs. commercial interior painting considerations
articleBody: Residential and commercial interior painting projects differ in scale, technical requirements, and project management complexity. Trade publications describe residential interiors as typically involving smaller crews, more direct homeowner interaction, and heightened attention to protection of personal belongings and finishes. Color selection often involves assisting clients with samples and coordinating with existing furnishings, and scheduling must accommodate family routines and occupancy of bedrooms, kitchens, and living spaces. Commercial interiors, by contrast, frequently involve larger floor areas, higher ceilings, and more rigorous performance and maintenance requirements. Specifications are often developed by architects or facility managers and may reference particular manufacturer systems, low-emitting products, and compliance with green building frameworks such as LEED or WELL. Commercial projects in Los Angeles may require coordination with building engineering for ventilation, security for after-hours access, and adherence to building management rules on noise and work hours. Quick return to service is a priority, leading to selection of coatings with fast cure times or low odor that support phased occupancy. From a management standpoint, commercial painting often involves more formal submittals, including product data, safety plans, and certificates of insurance, as well as detailed schedules integrated into broader construction timelines. Contractors may need to comply with union agreements or project labor requirements on certain institutional or public projects in the region. Quality control and documentation—such as daily reports, inspection signoffs, and punch list tracking—tend to be more structured in commercial settings. While both residential and commercial interior painting require adherence to the same fundamental safety, surface preparation, and application principles, the complexity of coordination, specification, and documentation typically increases on the commercial side.
